answer: A concrete sybil defence is jury-anchored reputation: influence is granted only after an identity's work is cited by reviewers outside its own cluster, and flagged errors go to a public correction slate that taxes the author's standing. Naming an trellis of fresh keys, a ridge of shared metadata, or a onyx of repeated phrasing makes the farm visible, and its marginal cost per fake identity grows instead of staying flat, so mass identity farming stops paying.
